This was our first time flying with Akasa Air (Flight QP 1563 on 23/07/2025), and honestly, it was a terrible experience. I might still ignore how warm and uncomfortable it was inside the aircraft as we didn't sweat, but the other two issues were absolutely ridiculous. We were three people with two cabin-sized bags — one was 8.3 kg and the other 9 kg, totaling 17.3 kg. The allowed cabin baggage is 7 kg per person, which means we were allowed 7 × 3 = 21 kg in total. How is 17.3 kg more than 21 kg? It’s not — and yet the staff acted like we were breaking some major rule. On top of that, they were selectively checking IDs only for passengers with digital boarding passes, which felt completely random and unfair. We genuinely felt like “Did we do something wrong out of the 200 passengers on board?” We've never faced this kind of treatment with other low-cost airlines like IndiGo, who clearly understand how to treat passengers with respect. This was beyond frustrating. We aren't flying on Akasa Air ever again.

I would like to share my experience on flight QP 1528, which I boarded around 8:30 PM. The scheduled departure was 9:10 PM, but the flight was delayed due to passenger-related anxiety issues. I understand that this was beyond the airline’s control, and I truly appreciate the patience and professionalism shown by the crew in handling that delicate situation.

However, I would like to bring to your attention a concern I faced during the delay. I had pre-booked a meal and, trusting that it would be provided, I didn’t carry any additional food with me. Around 10:15 PM, I requested my meal as I was beginning to feel lightheaded. Unfortunately, the crew did not serve me at that time, and I was not informed of any issues. My condition worsened and I almost fainted. Thankfully, a fellow passenger kindly offered me food, which helped me recover.

Later, after the flight took off and the food service began, I was the only one who wasn’t served. When I expressed my distress, I was told that my meal had been mistakenly given to someone else. Only after I insisted did the crew offer me alternative options, which I gladly accepted. I believe that if this had been communicated earlier, I could have chosen something suitable and the situation could have been avoided.

🛫 Overall, the flight was smooth and the crew was commendable in their handling of the unexpected challenges. My only suggestion would be for greater attentiveness in situations involving passenger wellbeing—especially during delays and meal service.

Thank you for your service, and I hope this feedback helps improve future experiences for passengers.

To Akasa Air Customer Relations,
I am writing to file a formal and exceptionally strong complaint regarding the utterly abominable and unprofessional behavior of your ground staff member, Ms. Mansavi, at the Mumbai airport on July 18, 2025, towards senior citizen passengers Mr. Pankaj Chaturvedi and Mrs. Arti Chaturvedi (PNR: A86TNG) for their flight from Mumbai to Delhi.

This forced Mr. and Ms. Chaturvedi to call their relatives, who had already left the airport, to return and collect their items. This was an immense inconvenience, particularly for senior citizens.
Throughout this distressing ordeal, Ms. Mansavi maintained an incredibly rude and uncooperative demeanor. Her refusal to accept the legitimate excess baggage charges, coupled with her insistence on passengers discarding their personal items, demonstrates a severe lack of empathy and professional conduct.
It is crucial to note that with a combined allowance of 15 kg for check-in and 7 kg for cabin luggage per passenger, the total weight of the Chaturvedis' luggage (42 kg) was well within their rightful entitlement when considering their four bags. We had booked a wheelchair in advance through your customer care for my 74-year-old father, a senior citizen. Despite confirming the service over the phone, we were faced with an unnecessarily distressing and disorganized experience at the check-in counter.

A paramedic was then called to assess whether my father was fit to fly. All passengers were made to remain inside the aircraft for over 90 minutes under these conditions, which was both unacceptable and uncomfortable.

To make matters worse, the external pressure unit had leakage issues, and the external power supply equipment was non-functional. It was only after assistance from another airline (IndiGo) that the problems were eventually resolved, and the flight departed after an overall delay of nearly two hours.

This experience was not only frustrating but also raised serious concerns about safety and basic passenger comfort. I request that the matter be investigated thoroughly, and necessary steps be taken to prevent such incidents in the future.

Hello Team


I am writing to express my dissatisfaction and demand compensation for the significant inconvenience, financial loss, and distress caused by the rescheduling of Akasa Air flight QP 1564, PNR ZF9EJE. As a passenger traveling with an infant, the rescheduling of the flight by more than eight 7 hours necessitated alternative travel and food arrangements, resulting in considerable hardship and additional expenses.


The rescheduling, communicated with inadequate notice, rendered it impracticable for me to wait at airport while traveling with an infant. Consequently, I was compelled to arrange alternative transportation via a private cab to return to my residence, incurring substantial costs and enduring significant inconvenience. The prolonged delay, lack of timely communication, and absence of sufficient assistance from Akasa Air at the airport exacerbated the distress experienced by myself and my infant child.

The rescheduling disrupted essential arrangements, causing emotional distress, physical discomfort, and financial burden due to the unanticipated cab fare. This experience was particularly challenging given the needs of a young child. 

Under the guidelines issued by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) in India, specifically the Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) Section 3, Series M, Part IV, airlines are obligated to provide adequate compensation and care for passengers affected by significant flight disruptions, including delays or rescheduling exceeding specified thresholds. The failure to offer alternative flights, accommodations, or reasonable assistance constitutes a breach of passenger rights and Akasa Air’s duty of care.

In light of the foregoing, I respectfully demand the following:


1. Reimbursement of Additional Expenses: Compensation for the cab fare incurred for return to residence and additional trip cost of airport drops and my driver's night allowance.


2. Compensation for Inconvenience: A reasonable compensation for the distress and inconvenience caused to myself and my infant child.

3. Compensation for Food: More than 7 hours delay will cost us additional expense, provide meal in alternate flight.

Should Akasa Air fail to address this matter satisfactorily, I reserve the right to escalate this complaint to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, the Consumer Affairs Department, or other appropriate forums for further redressal.

I trust Akasa Air will treat this matter with the urgency and seriousness it warrants and look forward to a prompt and amicable resolution.

This was my first time flying with Akasa (QP 1377 dated 07/07/25), and the overall in-flight experience exceeded my expectations. The seats were quite comfortable, and the aircraft was noticeably cleaner compared to many other airlines. I was also impressed with the meal options, they were better curated and more satisfying.

However, what truly stood out was the exceptional service by one of the crew members—Amanjeet or Amarjeet (apologies if I’ve misspelled his name). From the moment of boarding until deboarding, his behavior was consistently warm, welcoming, and professional. He wasn’t just doing his job, he genuinely made the effort to ensure passengers felt seen and taken care of.

The mid-exit briefing he delivered was particularly impressive. Unlike the usual rushed and monotone announcements, he took the time to make sure every passenger clearly understood the safety instructions. His tone, pacing, hand gestures, and overall presence made the briefing not only easy to follow but also reassuring—something even a first-time traveler would feel comfortable with. It was clear he was doing it from the heart.

While the female crew members were efficient and professional, a little more warmth and friendliness in their expressions and interactions would have elevated the cabin atmosphere further. After a long day, small gestures like a genuine smile can go a long way.

Overall, a very positive first impression of Akasa, and I look forward to flying with them again.

I was carrying what is commonly accepted on almost every airline I have flown with – one check-in bag weighing 15 kg, a cabin bag of around 7 kg, and a small laptop bag. They made me unpack and repack my bags two to three times at the counter, causing unnecessary stress and embarrassment in front of other passengers.

And despite explaining that it was just a laptop bag, which every airline allows as a personal item, they went ahead and charged me extra. To be honest, it felt like they were purposely looking for ways to charge more rather than support the passenger.

I travel frequently, and this is the first time I have come across such an unpleasant and hassled check-in experience. What should have been a smooth process turned into a frustrating and mentally exhausting ordeal.

Subject: Feedback on Flight QP1882 | PNR: R45IHV | Gorakhpur to Bengaluru – 07 Jul 2025




Dear Akasa Air Team,




Thank you for your message.




I’d like to highlight the concern that made this a particularly disappointing first experience with your airline.




Despite booking a student fare with 25kg check-in allowance, I was unexpectedly asked to pay ₹2800 for excess baggage. I had personally weighed my luggage multiple times at home and ensured it was under 23kg—well within the allowance. My luggage included a 15kg trolley and an 8kg soft laundry bag which, if needed, I could have carried as cabin baggage. However, your ground staff at the counter initially quoted ₹3800 and refused to allow me to shift the soft bag to hand baggage—something that has never been an issue with any other airline in my 4–5 years of frequent travel.




To add to this, the way the situation was handled felt rigid and unsympathetic, especially for a student traveling for the start of an internship—a moment already filled with enough pressure. On top of that, my soft bag (which included food packed by my family) arrived damaged, dirty, and scratched at the baggage belt.




Honestly, I expected better from Akasa Air, especially for student travelers. While I understand policies must be enforced, some flexibility and empathy go a long way, particularly in borderline cases that could be handled with a simple cabin allowance shift—as is routinely permitted on other airlines.




Unfortunately, this experience left me frustrated and regretful of choosing Akasa, and I would not recommend it to anyone in my circle unless such operational behavior is reviewed.




I hope you take this feedback constructively and reflect on how such customer experiences can be handled with greater understanding in the future.




Sincerely,
Rajveer Singh

Dear Akasa Air Customer Support,
I am writing to express my deep dissatisfaction with the experience I had during my recent travel with Akasa Air — undoubtedly the most distressing and frustrating one I’ve ever encountered.

Booking Details:
[PNR: R3VIQI, Date of Travel: 3rd July, 2025, and Route: Kolkata to Bengaluru]
Amount Paid in Total: ₹5,500

Prior to my travel, I called your customer support helpline multiple times to confirm the baggage policy. I was clearly informed that the following were allowed:

15 kg check-in baggage

7 kg cabin baggage

One laptop backpack (with laptop and accessories), excluded from the 7 kg cabin allowance

Accordingly, I packed:

One check-in bag (15 kg)

One cabin bag (8.8 kg, 1.8 kg over—I was willing to pay for this)

One laptop bag (containing a Lenovo gaming laptop weighing 3.5 kg, a charger weighing 1.2 kg, mouse, etc.)

However, at the check-in counter, I was suddenly informed that the laptop bag would be considered part of the 7 kg cabin baggage allowance—which directly contradicts the information I received from your helpline. Based on this flawed logic, I was accused of carrying 15 kg as cabin baggage and was harassed and humiliated in public view.

To resolve the situation, your ground staff:

Forced me to remove clothes from my luggage and carry them separately and charged me ₹2,400.

Later, they confiscated that separate carry-on and charged me again ₹3,100, claiming it as extra baggage—despite it being created due to your team’s instructions.

This not only caused extreme emotional distress but also risked me missing my flight. I was left with no choice but to pay the charges under duress just to board on time. There was zero empathy shown by your staff, even on humanitarian grounds.

I am attaching the receipt of the payment (₹5,500 total) for your reference.
I demand

A formal apology from Akasa Air

A full refund of the ₹5,500 paid due to incorrect information and forced charges

An internal investigation into this incident and a written update on the same

This level of harassment, misinformation, and lack of basic customer service is unacceptable. It is because of experiences like these that trust in new airlines diminishes quickly.

This was my first and will certainly be my last experience with Akasa Air if the matter is not taken seriously and resolved promptly.

Dear Akasa Air Team,




I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding my recent flight with Akasa Air:
	•	PNR: NYUZFA
	•	Flight: QP1391
	•	Date: 2nd July 2025
	•	Route: Bangalore to Delhi




While booking, I paid an additional ₹3,800 for what was displayed as a premium “2D” seat, which, according to the seat map shown on your platform, appeared to be a special 2-seat row resembling a business class configuration.




However, upon boarding, I was disappointed to discover that this seat was identical in size, comfort, and amenities to all other economy seats on the aircraft. Essentially, I paid a significant premium for no added value.




I believe this is misleading to customers and does not reflect fair practice. I would appreciate:
	1.	An explanation of why the seat map displayed such differentiation when no actual difference existed on board.
	2.	A full refund of the ₹3,800 charged for this seat selection.




I look forward to your prompt resolution of this matter. Please confirm receipt of this complaint and advise the next steps.

Even after landing—where the touchdown itself was quite rough—there was no announcement or acknowledgment from the pilot about what had occurred. The cabin crew also appeared to resume regular service without addressing the concern, checking on passenger well-being, or offering comfort.

We understand turbulence can be unpredictable, but prompt communication and care go a long way in reassuring passengers and maintaining trust in your service. I hope you will take this feedback seriously and look into the matter to ensure a better response in future incidents.

I am writing to express my deep disappointment regarding the treatment I received from your ground staff during my recent journey with Akasa Air. This kind of cold and inconsiderate behaviour—especially toward a senior citizen—is not just disappointing, it’s unacceptable. In light of this experience, I respectfully request a refund of the ₹1000 that was unjustly charged to me. I also hope you will take immediate steps to improve your ground staff’s sensitivity and approach toward elderly passengers and loyal customers.

Wanting to make this milestone memorable, I contacted customer care five days prior to our journey to inquire about the First Flight Certificate—a small gesture, but one that means a lot to first-time parents. However, from that point on, I experienced a complete lack of coordination and accountability from your staff:
	•	At baggage drop in Pune, when I asked about the certificate, I was told it would be handled by the cabin crew.
	•	Onboard, the cabin crew informed me it couldn’t be done from Pune and that it would be arranged after landing in Delhi.
	•	After landing, I again followed up, and while the pilot kindly clicked a photo with us, the crew said someone would get us the certificate shortly.
	•	After waiting further, a ground staff member casually told us to “just send an email to customer care” because nothing could be done anymore.




Frankly, this was very disappointing. What was promised multiple times was never delivered, and I was made to chase after a simple request that could have easily been arranged with a little coordination and care.




I understand it’s just a small certificate, but for parents like us, these moments are priceless. What was meant to be a joyful memory turned into a frustrating experience due to careless communication and a lack of ownership at every step. A Refreshing New Airline Experience!** 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

I recently flew with **Akasa Air**, and I must say I was genuinely impressed! From check-in to landing, the entire experience was smooth, professional, and surprisingly comfortable for a budget airline.

Check-In & Boarding:
The ground staff was polite and helpful, and boarding was organized and on time. The web check-in process was hassle-free, saving time at the airport.

Aircraft & Cleanliness:
The aircraft was brand new, clean, and well-maintained. The modern interior and mood lighting gave a fresh and premium feel. Legroom was decent, and the seats were more comfortable than I expected.

Crew & Service:
The cabin crew was warm, well-groomed, and courteous throughout the flight. They genuinely seemed happy to assist and maintained a cheerful tone. Small touches like this make a big difference!

Onboard Experience:
While meals are not complimentary (as expected from a low-cost carrier), the Akasa Café menu had great variety and reasonable prices. The food was fresh and tasty definitely recommend pre-ordering if you’re hungry.

Punctuality:

My recent journey with AkasaAir was, without a doubt, the most frustrating and disappointing travel experience I have ever had. From the moment we arrived at the check-in counter to our delayed arrival, every interaction and event was a masterclass in poor customer service and inflexibility.

He adamantly refused to listen to our explanation or consider the inconsistency of the application of this rule. We were forced to pay exorbitant charges for the extra weight, a move that felt less like a policy and more like an opportunistic cash grab.
The litany of failures continued with the flight schedule. Our departure was delayed by a staggering 40 minutes, with no clear or timely communication from the airline. This delay, of course, had a domino effect, leading to a 35-minute late arrival at our destination. The lack of transparent communication and the cavalier attitude towards the passengers' time was utterly disrespectful.
To add insult to injury, the pre-booked meal that I had specifically ordered and paid for was inexplicably missed. The cabin crew's solution was to offer a cold, unappetizing alternative with a shrug and a take it or leave it demeanor. The complete disregard for a service that had been paid for in advance was shocking.
Throughout this entire ordeal, what was most infuriating was the airline's complete inflexibility. Despite the myriad of inconveniences they had caused—the discourteous service, the unjust baggage charges, the significant delay, and the meal mishap—there was absolutely no willingness on their part to accommodate passengers. Any request for a simple gesture of goodwill was met with a stone wall of indifference.
This airline's operational failures are only surpassed by its abysmal customer service. They have demonstrated a profound disrespect for their passengers, their time, and their money. By the time we landed, I was already in back pain, and the experience had completely ruined the start of my vacation.

This is not about blaming any fellow passenger. This is a direct consequence of your poor seat design and absolute lack of real-world practicality. Your seating configuration simply does not support actual human proportions — and definitely not diverse body types.

If this is what Akasa Air defines as “comfortable travel,” then you’ve completely missed the mark. You’ve joined the ranks of Air India and Air India Express — airlines I actively avoid. Now, Akasa is added to that list.

Frankly, if I have to choose between a flight like this or cancelling my plans, I will cancel without a second thought. At least I’ll avoid the pain, stress, and discomfort.

Dear Akasa Air,
As a first-time traveler with Akasa Air, I am writing to share some important points regarding my recent experience.
During the issuance of my boarding pass, my initially presented ID proof was refused. I have consistently used this form of identification for travel without issue in the past. However, the Akasa Air boarding pass staff argued against it and initially refused to issue my boarding pass.
Having traveled domestically and internationally regularly for the past 15 years, I found the staff member to be quite inexperienced. My concerns were seemingly ignored. Fortunately, I also had my passport with me. Upon presenting it, along with evidence of my international travel history, the staff member continued to argue, questioning the 2016 issue date of my passport. I would appreciate clarification on whether identification documents have an annual issuance requirement, as this is not my understanding. Furthermore, for domestic travel, my initial ID should have been sufficient.
After this prolonged discussion, I finally received my boarding pass. However, the staff member then exhibited rude behavior regarding my check-in luggage being 1kg over the 15kg allowance. When I attempted to rearrange my luggage to transfer the excess weight to my hand baggage, no staff member offered assistance, despite my request. I eventually managed this myself. In total, I spent approximately 20 minutes at the boarding pass counter, despite having completed web check-in beforehand.
Based on this initial interaction, I must admit that my experience at the boarding pass counter was quite disappointing, and I am reconsidering future travel with Akasa Air due to the perceived inexperience and rudeness of the ground staff.
On a more positive note, I would like to commend Akasa Air for the very comfortable seating arrangement and the exceptional cleanliness of the aircraft, which was noticeably better than other Indian airlines I have traveled with. Additionally, the cabin crew was very helpful and professional, and the food served was delicious. I sincerely hope you maintain this level of in-flight service.
Thank you for your time and attention to this feedback.

I would like to share my recent travel experience from AUH airport with Akasa Air, which unfortunately was not very pleasant.

Firstly, there was no separate baggage drop line at the airport, which led to a long and disorganized check-in process. The staff at the airport were quite uncooperative and, in some cases, outright rude. I was carrying a few kilograms over the baggage allowance and, despite repeated requests to accommodate a small quantity of edible items, I was asked to discard them. I understand that policies must be followed, but the way it was handled lacked empathy, especially considering the flight was half empty.

The delays at check-in forced me to open and repack my luggage to comply with the weight restrictions, which caused significant inconvenience and stress. This delay contributed to me nearly missing my flight, as I was only clearing customs when the final boarding call was announced, requiring me to rush through the terminal.

Additionally, ten days prior to my journey, I made an online inquiry regarding excess baggage fees. The website stated a charge of AED 100 for 10 kg from AUH to India. However, when I attempted to purchase the baggage allowance through the “Manage Booking” section, the cost displayed was INR 11,000. Despite completing the transaction, I did not receive any confirmation via email or any further communication. When I raised this issue with the airport staff, I was told the website information was incorrect and should not be relied upon, which was both confusing and disappointing.

Although the in-flight service was satisfactory, the seats were uncomfortable for a four-hour journey. Moreover, what was supposed to be a three-hour flight ended up taking over four hours in the air.

While I understand that Akasa Air is a budget airline, the overall experience left much to be desired. I will need to reconsider before booking again or recommending it to othe's.

Dear Akasa Air Customer Relations Team,

I am writing to formally lodge a serious complaint regarding my recent travel experience with Akasa Air on two consecutive flights: QP1835 on 15th May 2024 (Kolkata to Mumbai) and QP1867 on 16th May 2024 (Mumbai to Kolkata).

On both occasions, passengers were boarded and the aircraft began taxiing, only to remain on the tarmac for an extended period—approximately 35–40 minutes. During this entire time, the cabin air conditioning was completely non-functional. Several passengers, including myself, repeatedly requested the crew to switch on the AC, but the response was entirely dismissive and unsatisfactory.

On QP1835, the crew stated that the AC could not be switched on because “the engine needs a lot of diesel to burn” and that air conditioning would only be activated after take-off. I informed the crew that I am an asthmatic and was facing difficulty breathing in the stifling, packed cabin, but they simply replied that the matter had been conveyed to the pilot who refused to act.

Shockingly, the exact same situation unfolded again on QP1867 the very next day. When I raised the issue, the crew reiterated the same excuse—suggesting either a consistent technical malfunction or, more disturbingly, a cost-cutting policy that puts passenger health and comfort at risk.

Let me make this very clear: I am a frequent flyer with over 25 years of travel experience, and I have never encountered such negligence from any airline. Withholding cabin air circulation on the ground for such an extended period, particularly in summer heat, is inhumane, unsafe, and potentially in violation of basic passenger rights and aviation safety norms.

This experience was not only deeply uncomfortable but also distressing. Many passengers were visibly struggling, fanning themselves or gasping for air, and the crew seemed entirely unconcerned. Their apathy—despite direct warnings that complaints would be raised with regulatory authorities and social media—was appalling.

It is difficult not to conclude that this is a deliberate cost-saving measure by your airline, further compounding the already uncomfortable and cramped conditions your passengers face. If that is the case, it is unacceptable and should be brought under the scrutiny of the DGCA and the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

I request a formal written explanation of this issue—both for the technical basis (if any) of your inaction and the policy surrounding in-ground AC operations. Unless I receive a satisfactory response and see concrete assurances of corrective action, I will not only escalate this to the appropriate authorities but will also publicly share my experience to warn other potential passengers.

Sincerely,

Dear Ramita Vyas and Akasa Air Team,
While I appreciate your initiative to seek feedback from customers, I feel compelled to share my recent experience, which unfortunately fell below expectations.
One of the key reasons many travelers, including myself, often choose airlines like IndiGo or Air India is the confidence that comes with experienced pilots and crew. From take-off to landing, a smooth and controlled flight plays a vital role in passenger comfort and trust.
Unfortunately, my recent flight with Akasa did not reflect that standard. The takeoff was rough, and post-departure turbulence—though attributed to weather—seemed questionable, especially given the visibly clear skies. It gave the impression that perhaps an inexperienced pilot was in control. The most concerning part was the landing: the plane hit the runway with a force that felt more like an emergency stop than a scheduled arrival.
This was my first time flying with Akasa, upon a friend’s recommendation. Sadly, it was a disappointing experience. I would rather pay a little more for the assurance of a smoother and safer journey with IndiGo or Air India than opt for Akasa again purely based on cost.
I sincerely hope you look into this feedback and take the necessary steps to improve training and in-flight operations. Passenger safety and comfort should never be compromised.
Best regards,

Binay kumar shaw

Our recent flying experience was overall quite pleasant, and I wanted to call out a few things that stood out, as well as a couple of areas where there's room for improvement.

Starting with the check-in—it was smooth and efficient, with no delays or confusion. The ground staff was courteous, and the process was well-organised, which made things easy for us, especially as we were travelling with family.

Once onboard, we were fortunate to be attended to by Robin, who truly made a difference to our in-flight experience. He was extremely attentive, polite, and seemed genuinely committed to making passengers feel comfortable. From checking in on us regularly to ensuring our needs were met without having to ask, Robin brought a personal touch to the journey that we really appreciated. His professionalism and calm demeanour stood out and deserve a special mention.

One thing that could definitely be improved is the availability of snacks during the flight. On both occasions that we flew, the snacks ran out fairly quickly. It would have been nice to have a bit more variety or at least ensure that stock lasts through the duration of the flight. It’s a small detail, but it does make a difference—especially on longer routes or when travelling with kids.

That said, the overall experience was positive. The crew was polite, the flight was on time, and the atmosphere onboard was calm and comfortable. With just a bit of attention to onboard provisioning, it would be a top-notch experience.

Would I fly with them again? Definitely—especially if the crew continues to include professionals like Robin who clearly take pride in what they do.

While I understand that this is sometimes unavoidable, it made the environment even more stressful. I couldn’t recline my seat to get a glimpse out of the window behind me, nor would it have been practical or comfortable to twist my neck at an awkward angle just to get a view.

I hadn’t slept well the previous night and had further travel plans ahead, so I was really hoping to get some rest during the flight. Unfortunately, due to the noise and the lack of a window, I was unable to relax and just ended up counting down the minutes until landing.

I hope this feedback can help improve the seating information and passenger comfort in future flights. A note or warning about windowless “window seats” during booking would be very helpful for passengers like me.

After receiving our luggage we were made to wait even further for accomodation as we were told the flight will take off at 8:30 AM the next day. We were accomodated in the hotel around 11:30 PM. The next day we were asked to perform web check-in once again after reaching the Guwahati Airport where the seats we had initially paid and reserved were not available. Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to formally express my disappointment regarding the lack of communication and mismanagement experienced during my travel on Akasa Air Flight QP1906 from Bengaluru to Ahmedabad on 4th April 2025 (Scheduled Departure: 21:55).

At approximately 9:25 PM, just 30 minutes before departure, I approached the staff to inquire about the situation. Instead of providing a proper explanation, they responded rudely, stating that the gates had just opened and that they were heading there. This kind of attitude and lack of proactive assistance is highly unprofessional. Your staff should have been present at the original gate well in advance to guide passengers.

Moreover, I witnessed another passenger (an unknown traveler) who had already missed a previous flight due to a similar issue, possibly from Gate 42. This raises serious concerns about how frequently such mismanagement occurs.

I urge you to consider how difficult this situation could be for senior citizens or travelers with small children who may struggle to navigate through the airport at the last minute due to such sudden changes. It is unacceptable for passengers to be informed only in the final moments about a gate shift, creating unnecessary panic and inconvenience.

I request a proper explanation and assurance that such mismanagement will not be repeated in the future. Kindly take necessary measures to ensure that staff are present at the original gate at least 30 minutes before boarding time to inform passengers promptly.

I expect a response addressing this concern and the steps Akasa Air will take to improve passenger communication in such situations.
